# Volume 1 — CHAPTER XX. A Good Imagination Gone Wrong

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

SPRING had arrived again at Grey Shutters—that lovely, fickle, hesitant Canadian spring, which drifted through April and May as a series of delightful, crisp, cool days featuring rosy sunsets and wonders of rebirth and expansion. Red buds appeared on the maples along Linger Lane, while tiny unfurling ferns emerged near the Nymph’s Well. Far off in the barrens, past Mr. Silas Mott’s property, the Mayflowers bloomed, revealing pink and white stars of fragrant beauty beneath their brown foliage. Every schoolboy and schoolgirl spent one glorious afternoon picking them, returning in the luminous, resonant dusk with arms and baskets laden with floral treasures.
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0000 }

“My heart aches for those who reside in places lacking Mayflowers,” Nell remarked. “According to Isolde, they might possess something superior, yet nothing superior to Mayflowers could exist, could it, Thirza? Furthermore, Isolde claims that if individuals are unaware of what Mayflowers are like, they do not yearn for them. Nevertheless, I believe that represents the most mournful aspect of all. It strikes me as tragic, Thirza, to be ignorant of Mayflowers and consequently not long for them. Are you aware of my belief regarding Mayflowers, Thirza? My idea is that they represent the spirits of the blossoms that perished during the previous summer, with this being their paradise. However, our day was marvelous, Thirza. Our midday meal was consumed down within a large, moss-covered depression beside an ancient well—a place of such romance. Wilfred Mott challenged Arty Pettigrew to leap across it, a feat Arty performed since he refused to back down from a challenge. Within the school, no one would ever refuse. Challenging others is currently quite popular. Every Mayflower discovered by Mr. Pidgeon was presented to Sukey Pullen, and I overheard him utter ‘sweets to the sweet.’ That phrase originated from a book, I am certain; nevertheless, it demonstrates that he possesses a degree of imagination. Mayflowers were extended to me as well, but I turned them down contemptuously. The identity of that individual cannot be revealed because I pledged that their name would never pass my lips. Wreaths were fashioned from the Mayflowers and placed upon our hats; then, as the hour arrived to return, we paraded along the roadway in pairs, bearing our flowers and headpieces while singing ‘My Home on the Hill.’ Oh, the excitement was immense, Thirza. The entire household of Mr. Silas Mott hurried outside to observe us, and every person we encountered along the path halted and gazed at our retreating figures. We truly created a stir.”
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0001 }

“Not much wonder! Such silly doings!” Thirza replied.
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0002 }

Following the Mayflowers, violets appeared, covering Primrose Dell in shades of purple. Nell passed through the dell on her route to school using respectful strides and admiring eyes, just like she was walking upon sacred earth.
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0003 }

“In a way,” she said to Isolde, “passing through this place makes me feel indifferent to whether Hughie—or anyone else—passes me in school. Once I am up in school, though, everything changes and my concern is just as strong as before. I seem to contain so many distinct Annes. That might explain why I cause so much trouble, or so I occasionally believe. Life would be far simpler if I were merely the single Nell, yet it would not be nearly as intriguing.”
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0004 }

On an evening in June, as the orchard trees bore pink blooms once more, as the frogs sang with a sweet, metallic clarity within the swamps near the upper end of the Lake of Glassy Waters, and the breeze carried the rich scents of fir forests and clover meadows, Nell occupied a seat at her gable window. Though she had been reviewing her schoolwork, reading became impossible in the fading light, prompting her to drift into a open-eyed daydream while gazing beyond the branches of the Frost Maiden, which were decorated again with clusters of flowers.
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0005 }

In every fundamental way, the small gable room remained the same. The walls retained their whiteness, the pincushion its hardness, and the chairs their rigid, yellow uprightness. Nevertheless, the room’s entire atmosphere had transformed. A new, dynamic, pulsing presence filled the space, appearing to saturate it while remaining entirely distinct from the schoolgirl books, garments, ribbons, and even the chipped blue pitcher holding apple blossoms on the table. It seemed that every dream, both slumbering and conscious, belonging to its vibrant inhabitant had assumed a clear yet intangible shape, adorning the plain room like magnificent, sheer fabrics woven from rainbows and moonlight. Before long, Thirza entered smartly, carrying a few of Nell’s aprons that had just been ironed for school. Draping them across a chair, she took a seat and let out a brief sigh. That afternoon she had suffered from a headache, and even though the ache had subsided, she experienced weakness and felt “tuckered out,” to use her own phrase. Nell gazed upon her, her eyes clear with compassion.
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0006 }

“I sincerely desire that I might have suffered the headache instead of you, Thirza. For your sake, I would have borne it with joy.”
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0007 }

“I suppose you accomplished your role by taking care of the chores and allowing me to sleep,” Thirza remarked. “It appears you managed reasonably well and committed fewer errors than you typically do. Naturally, starching Obed’s handkerchiefs was not precisely required! Furthermore, when the majority of individuals place a pie inside the oven to heat for dinner, they remove it to consume once it becomes hot, rather than abandoning it until it is incinerated. However, that clearly does not appear to be how you do things.”
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0008 }

Thirza was consistently rendered rather acerbic whenever she suffered from headaches.
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0009 }

“Oh, I’m so sorry,” Nell said contritely. “From the instant I placed that pie in the oven until this moment, it completely slipped my mind, even though I had an intuitive feeling that the dinner table lacked something. When you placed me in control this morning, I had fully made up my mind not to invent anything in my head, but to focus my mind entirely on reality. Things went fairly smoothly until the pie went into the oven, but after that, I was overcome by a powerful urge to pretend to be an enchanted princess imprisoned inside an isolated tower, while a good-looking knight mounted on a jet-black horse rode to save me. That explains why the pie was forgotten by me. I was unaware that I had starched the handkerchiefs. During the entire time I spent ironing, my mind was occupied trying to invent a title for a new island that Isolde and I found further up the brook. It is an utterly delightful place, Thirza. A pair of maple trees grows on it, and it is completely encircled by the flowing brook. Finally, the thought hit me that naming it Victoria Island would be grand, since its discovery occurred on the Regent’s birthday. Isolde and I are both extremely loyal. Even so, I feel bad regarding the pie and those handkerchiefs. Because today is an anniversary, I wished to behave exceptionally well. Are you able to recall the event that occurred on this date one year ago, Thirza?”
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0010 }

“No, I am unable to recall any particular thing.”
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0011 }

“Oh, Thirza, that was the date of my arrival at Grey Shutters. That moment will remain with me forever. My whole existence pivoted then. Naturally, you would not view it as being so significant. A year has passed during my time here, bringing me immense happiness. To be sure, difficulties have arisen, yet such hardships are overcome through living. Do you regret having retained me, Thirza?”
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0012 }

“No, I am unable to claim that I feel regret,” stated Thirza, who occasionally pondered how it was possible she had existed prior to Nell’s arrival at Grey Shutters, “no, not precisely regretful. Should your studies be complete, Nell, my desire is for you to hurry across to inquire whether Mrs. Pembroke would be willing to allow me the use of Isolde’s apron pattern.”
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0013 }

“Oh—it is—it is far too dark,” Nell exclaimed.
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0014 }

“Excessively dark? How so, when it is merely dusk. Furthermore, Heaven knows you have crossed frequently enough once night has fallen.”
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0015 }

“In the early morning, I will go over,” Nell said with enthusiasm. “Thirza, I will wake at sunrise and head over.”
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0016 }

“What has taken hold of your mind now, Nell Harcourt? I desire that pattern to cut your new apron this evening. Go immediately and be quick as well.”
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0017 }

“Then I will need to take the long way by the road,” Nell said, picking up her hat with hesitation.
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0018 }

“Travel along the path and lose thirty minutes! I want to overtake you!”
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0019 }

“Thirza, I am unable to pass through the Whispering Wood,” Nell exclaimed in desperation.
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0020 }

Thirza gazed.
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0021 }

“The Whispering Wood! Have you lost your mind? What beneath the canopy could the Whispering Wood possibly be?”
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0022 }

“The spruce wood over the brook,” spoke Nell softly.
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0023 }

“Nonsense! A haunted forest doesn't exist at all. Who has been filling your head with those stories?”
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0024 }

“No one,” admitted Nell. “Isolde and I merely pictured that the wood was haunted. Every location in this vicinity is so—so—ordinary. We simply invented this for our personal entertainment. It was started by us in April. A haunted wood possesses such immense romance, Thirza. The spruce grove was chosen by us owing to its great gloominess. Oh, the most distressing things have been imagined by us. A white lady travels beside the brook at approximately this hour of the evening and wrings her hands and makes wailing noises. She makes an appearance whenever a death in the family is about to occur. Furthermore, the ghost belonging to a little slain child frequents the corner up near Larkrise; it sneaks up behind a person and touches your hand with its cold fingers—like this. Oh, Thirza, thinking about it makes me shiver. Also, a headless man strides up and down the track and skeletons glare at a person from between the branches. Oh, Thirza, I would not walk through the Whispering Wood after nightfall now for any reason. I would feel certain that pale figures would extend their arms from behind the trees and seize me.”
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0025 }

“Did anybody ever hear such a thing!” exclaimed Thirza, having heard this in speechless wonder. “Nell Harcourt, are you telling me that you actually credit all those evil absurdities born of your own mind?”
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0026 }

“I do not quite believe,” stammered Nell. “To be precise, I do not believe it while it is day. However, Thirza, things change once night falls. Spirits roam at that time.”
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0027 }

“Ghosts do not exist, Nell.”
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0028 }

“Oh, but there are, Thirza,” Nell cried with eagerness. “I am acquainted with folk who have witnessed them. Furthermore, they are reputable individuals. Wilfred Mott asserts that his grandmother observed his grandfather herding the cows home one evening, a year following his burial. You are aware that Wilfred Mott’s grandmother would not fabricate a tale under any circumstances. She is a highly devout woman. Additionally, Mrs. Thomas’s father was chased back to his house one evening by a fiery lamb whose severed head dangled by a piece of skin. He stated he recognized it as the ghost of his brother, serving as an omen that his own death would occur within nine days. While he did not perish then, his death happened two years later, which proves it was genuine. Also, Opal Pettigrew claims—”
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0029 }

“Nell Harcourt,” Thirza cut in with resolve, “I never wish to listen to you speaking like this anymore. I have harbored reservations regarding that imagination of yours all this time, and should it result in this, I will not tolerate any behavior of the sort. You will head straight across to Pembroke’s, and you will walk through that spruce grove, simply to serve as a lesson and a caution to you. And do not ever allow me to hear another remark from you concerning haunted woods.”
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0030 }

Nell could beg and weep all she wanted—and she indeed did, because her fear was extremely genuine. Her mind had gotten the best of her, causing her to view the spruce grove with fatal horror once darkness fell. Thirza, however, was unyielding. She led the cowering ghost-seer down to the spring and commanded her to go immediately across the bridge and enter the shadowy recesses of weeping women and decapitated phantoms on the other side.
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0031 }

“Oh, Thirza, how can you be so cruel?” wept Nell. “How would it make you feel if a white thing really grabbed me and hauled me away?”
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0032 }

“I am willing to chance it,” Thirza stated callously. “You are aware that I constantly stand by my words. I am going to stop you from picturing phantoms in places. Start walking, right now.”
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0033 }

Nell walked forward. To be exact, she tripped across the bridge and proceeded trembling along the dreadful, dark trail on the other side. That journey was something Nell never forgot. She deeply regretted allowing her imagination such freedom. Shadows all around her concealed the goblins she had envisioned, which stretched forth their icy, skeletal hands to seize the frightened little girl responsible for creating them. Her heart stopped beating when a pale piece of birch bark blew out of the ravine and onto the brown ground of the grove. Beads of sweat formed on her forehead at the sound of a protracted cry caused by two ancient branches grinding together. The bats diving above her in the dark seemed like the wings of otherworldly beings. Upon reaching the field belonging to Mr. William Bell, she ran across it as though chased by a host of white entities, and she came to the door of the Pembroke kitchen so breathless that the demand for the apron pattern could barely be gasped out by her. Because Isolde was absent, she possessed no reason to delay. Facing the terrifying trip back was unavoidable. Nell traversed it again with her eyes closed, choosing to chance smashing her head against the branches rather than chance beholding a white entity. As she at last tripped over the log bridge, a single extended, quivering breath of relief was drawn by her.
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0034 }

“Well, so you were not caught by anything?” Thirza said without sympathy.
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0035 }

“Oh, Mar—Thirza,” stammered Nell, “I’ll b-b-be sat-t-tisfied with ord-d-dinary locations following this.”
{: #nw-v01-c20-p0036 }
